sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Warren County
sections.html:
Warren County deeds go to the recorder at 406 Justice Drive, Lebanon, OH 45036, on the same campus as the auditor. Call 513-695-1382 or 513-695-1383. The fax line is 513-695-2949.

Make checks payable to the Warren County Recorder. The counter wants the exact amount and returns any short payment without recording it. Frequent filers are encouraged to open an escrow account so an over or under payment does not hold up a same-day recording. A typical filing is turned around in 24 hours.

The recorder's fee schedule is dated October 17, 2019 and tracks the amounts in Revised Code 317.32.

Selected Warren County recording fees
Document or serviceFee
First two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Copies made by staff$2.00
Subdivision plat, 24 by 36 inches$86.40 per page
Federal lien$5.00
Federal release$3.00
Zoning resolution$50.00
Zoning amendment$20.00
Financing statement (real estate only)$12.00
Each name indexed on a financing statement$4.00

The office does not charge the optional $5 digital preservation fee. If a filer sends the extra $5 anyway, the office keeps it instead of rejecting the paper for incorrect fees. Marginal notations that index earlier instruments carry no charge. Members of the public who copy documents themselves pay 25 cents per page.

Most documents have been online since April 20, 2016, and all deeds are indexed and viewable back to 1797. The search works best with the parcel number. The 10-digit parcel number appears in the upper left corner of an address or name search on the auditor's property site.

To save a copy, scroll to the bottom of the open document, click the print icon and use the PDF that opens. More than 5 million documents have been recorded in the county, and staff will help by phone at 513-695-1382.

  • E-recording works for every document type except plats.
  • Every land record must include a legal description.
  • A transfer document that needs to be re-recorded must be redone with new notarized signatures, a rule shared by the recorder and the auditor.
  • A free property fraud alert sends an email, text or phone message when a document is filed on a parcel you own. If you do not use a computer, call the office to sign up.

sections.h2: What the auditor requires before the recorder
sections.html:
Ohio makes the auditor transfer the deed first. The auditor's transfer page lists what must be in order, and a deed missing any item comes back to you.

  • A properly completed Statement of Value and Receipt (DTE Form 100), or a Statement of Reason for Exemption (DTE Form 100 EX), plus the fees payable to the Warren County Auditor.
  • A grantor name that matches the way the grantor took title in the prior deed.
  • A reference to the previous deed of record, written on the new deed.
  • Approval and initials from the map department before the deed is presented to the auditor.
  • Form DTE 102 when the parcel is, or last year was, in the CAUV farm program.
  • The grantor's signature, notarized.

The charges: $1.00 per thousand dollars of price as the mandatory state conveyance fee, $2.00 per thousand as the county's transfer tax, for a combined $3.00 per thousand, with leftover pennies bumped up to the next dime, plus $0.50 per parcel for the transfer itself. The county commissioners adopted the $2.00 levy, which is a permissive one.

sections.h2: Transfers exempt from the conveyance fee
sections.html:
An exempt transfer uses form 100 EX, where the grantee checks one reason from a lettered list on the back. Reasons (b), (g) and (m) need a notarized affidavit explaining the facts, since the auditor wants to know why no money changed hands.

Under section 319.54 the exempt categories include:

  • Transfers to or from governments and their agencies.
  • Deeds that exist only to secure or release a debt.
  • Confirmation and correction deeds.
  • Gifts between spouses and between parents and children.
  • Sales for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Deeds that put property into, or take it out of, a trust the maker can revoke.
  • Transfers among heirs when no consideration is paid.

The recorder indexes each document so a title examiner can trace the chain of ownership and see any debt against the parcel. Recording right after closing puts your buyer's deed in that chain. The permanent record is what makes it possible to buy land with a clear title.

Every Ohio deed needs the grantor's signature with a notary's certificate. Warren County treats the signature and acknowledgment as a precondition and will not take the deed without them.

Here is what to have ready on recording day: the notarized original deed with the auditor's endorsement, the parcel number, a check for the exact amount made out to the Warren County Recorder, and a prepaid envelope if you are mailing it. If your lender is paying off an old mortgage, ask the title company to confirm that the release will be recorded too. An unreleased mortgage can show up in the next title search and cause trouble for your buyer later. Filings sent by e-recording skip the envelope and the trip.

sections.h2: What the recorder keeps and what sits elsewhere
sections.html:
The county uses tract (geographical) indexing and has no registered land (Torrens) system. Staff do not sell blank forms. The office records military discharge papers (DD214). A mailed filing has to include return postage or a prepaid envelope.

People often arrive at this office for papers it does not hold. Vital records and court files sit with other departments:

  • Birth and death records: 513-695-1220.
  • Marriage licenses: 513-695-1183.
  • Divorce records: 513-695-1120.

sections.h2: Property tax on a home being sold
sections.html:
The county treasurer collects it, with office hours Monday through Friday from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm. Pay online through the myWarrenCountyOhio portal or by phone at 513-496-2931. Due dates are set each year, so ask the treasurer for the current ones.

If you have not paid, or your mortgage servicer pays from escrow, confirm the balance before closing day so the payoff and the deed fees can be settled together.

For a sale, plan the office stops in order: the treasurer for the tax balance, the map department and auditor for the transfer, then the recorder. A cash buyer skips the lender's paperwork, but the same deed steps apply, so bring the prior deed reference and a notary with you to avoid a return trip.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Warren County recorder?
faqs.a: Call 513-695-1382 or 513-695-1383, or write to 406 Justice Drive, Lebanon, OH 45036. The fax line is 513-695-2949, and documents typically turn around in about a day.

faqs.q: What is the Warren County fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule shows $34.00 for the opening two pages and $8.00 per page beyond that. The office does not collect the optional $5 preservation fee.
Yes, for every document type except plats. Paper filings still go to the counter at 406 Justice Drive with exact fees.

faqs.q: What happens if my check for Warren County recording is the wrong amount?
faqs.a: The document comes back unrecorded. The recorder requires exact fees and returns shortages, and it recommends an escrow account for filers who want over or under payments handled the same day.

faqs.q: How much is the Warren County transfer fee on a house sale?
faqs.a: The auditor charges $1.00 per thousand dollars as the mandatory conveyance fee plus $2.00 per thousand in county transfer tax, a combined $3.00 per thousand, and $0.50 per parcel to transfer it. The grantor pays these to the auditor before recording.
